targets.old_statement: Stop always halts fully while yield halts only when traffic demands, yet both yield right-of-way and both pick the stop line, crosswalk or sight point in the same order.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Stop always halts fully while yield halts only when traffic demands, yet both yield right-of-way and both pick the stop line, crosswalk or sight point in the same order.
targets.statement: A stop sign requires a full stop every time before yielding right-of-way—stopping before the stop line, else the crosswalk, else the nearest point with a view of cross traffic—whereas a yield sign requires slowing down, checking traffic, yielding right-of-way, and stopping fully only when traffic conditions require it.

targets.old_statement: Dead signals degrade to stop-sign behavior with right-of-way rules, the same fallback a flashing red gives, while officers can override both.
